tldr: After weeks of speculation about a stealth model topping community leaderboards, Z.ai confirmed "Ox Alpha" was actually GLM-5.3-Flash and shipped its weights. The model runs entirely on 100,000 domestic Chinese chips with no Nvidia hardware, at roughly 1/40 Opus 4.8's price.
whats_new: Z.ai's GLM inference build now runs on the full 100,000-chip domestic stack, and the company is in talks to bring it to overseas cloud providers.
why_it_matters: GLM-5.3-Flash is a working example of a frontier-tier model served entirely off Nvidia hardware at a fraction of Western pricing — a data point for any team evaluating non-Nvidia inference options or benchmarking against Chinese open-weight models.

status.state: Domestic-chip identity confirmed, scaling toward overseas hosting
status.reenable: no named overseas cloud provider yet
status.detail: The mystery "Ox Alpha" model turned out to be GLM-5.3-Flash, running on 100,000 domestic Chinese chips at a fraction of Western pricing; Z.ai is now in talks to bring that inference build to overseas cloud providers.

track.label: Ox Alpha unmasked as GLM-5.3-Flash, on domestic chips

beats.headline: Z.ai confirms the mystery "Ox Alpha" model is GLM-5.3-Flash, releases weights
beats.summary: After weeks of speculation about the unbranded "Ox Alpha" model topping community leaderboards, Z.ai confirms it's a new GLM-series release and ships GLM-5.3-Flash — a 320B-A18B MoE with a 1M-token context — as open weights.

beats.headline: GLM-5.3-Flash runs entirely on 100,000 domestic Chinese chips at 1/40 Opus 4.8's price — no Nvidia involved
beats.summary: Z.ai discloses the model behind Ox Alpha runs on a 100,000-chip domestic stack with no Nvidia hardware, at roughly 1/40 the price of Opus 4.8; Z.ai shares surge 8% on the news, while one outlet pushes back that the Chinese-chip framing is really about cost optimization, not a geopolitical statement.

beats.headline: Coverage settles on Z.ai's company background and reconfirms the Ox Alpha identity
beats.summary: Explainers catch readers up on who Z.ai is and reconfirm GLM-5.3-Flash as the model behind Ox Alpha.

beats.headline: GLM-5.3 closes the gap on Anthropic's cyber benchmark as usage climbs and the stealth-model framing draws scrutiny
beats.summary: Independent comparisons put GLM-5.3 near Anthropic on a cyber test and frame Ox Alpha as a real OpenAI-tier rival, while usage trackers show GLM-5.3-Flash topping global AI call volume and one piece notes the domestic-chip stack ran undetected for weeks.

beats.headline: GLM inference build reaches 100,000 domestic chips, Z.ai eyes overseas cloud providers
beats.summary: digitimes reports the GLM inference build now runs on 100,000 Chinese chips, with Z.ai in talks to bring it to overseas cloud providers.

open_questions: Which overseas cloud providers is Z.ai in talks with, and would hosting there still depend on the same domestic-chip supply?
Do independent evals corroborate GLM-5.3-Flash's claimed cost and benchmark advantage?
Is the 100,000-domestic-chip inference build reproducible at scale, or was it a one-time capacity showcase for the Ox Alpha reveal?
take_for_builders: If you're benchmarking non-Nvidia inference options, treat GLM-5.3-Flash's domestic-chip cost and throughput claims as a lead to verify independently, not a settled number.
